Hi Alex and Priya —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap + proposed next steps to validate model fit for your structured output use case: 

1) We'll run the pilot evals we discussed against your core prompt set (attached: prompt_set_v2.json) covering invoice-parsing and purchase-order normalization.
2) We'll validate function-calling compliance (JSON schema) and evaluate retry behaviors for partial failures.
3) We'll share a short benchmark (latency, token cost) across three model variants: rwd-ft-1, llama-3-16b-q4, and gpt-open-7b.

I've attached a baseline eval (eval_results.csv) and a sample schema (schema_example.json) so you can see what we'll check. Can you confirm the sample prompt set is the latest? Also, are there any regulatory constraints on storing inference logs for this project?

If that sounds good I’ll loop in Aditya to schedule a 60-min technical run-through next week and we’ll push the initial benchmark into your Drive link.

Best,

This looks right. Confirming the prompt_set_v2.json matches what our product team uses in staging. A couple of clarifications:

Marissa — copying the quick action items from the Acme thread so we can prep the runbook before the tech call.

Summary of asks from Alex/Priya:
- Strict JSON schema validation (no extra fields).
- Retry behavior simulation for partial response and idempotency checks.
- 90-day retention w/ encryption requirement if they need >90 days.

Proposed baseline evaluation steps (short):
1) Run prompt_set_v2 across three model configs: rwd-ft-1 (our fine-tuned variant for parsing), llama-3-16b-q4 (efficient open model), gpt-open-7b (higher-quality baseline). Capture token cost, mean latency @ p50/p90, and schema pass rate.
2) For schema validation: run outputs through jsonschema with strict additionalProperties=false; flag any coercions.
3) Retry sim: craft failure injection where the model returns truncated JSON; ensure the function-calling layer issues exactly one retry and that the final output is deterministic for the same input (idempotency key).
4) Produce a one-page summary and the full CSV (eval_results.csv) in the shared Drive link.

Open questions for the call:
- Do we need to run the eval under Dedicated capacity to match their latency SLOs? (this affects cost estimate)
- Any compliance documents to share ahead of time (SOC2, DPA)? We should prepare a short packet.

I’ll draft the runbook and a parameterized test harness. Neha — can you own the schema test harness and Dev — can you wire the retry injection into the function-calling wrapper?

-Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Got it —

I’ll build the strict jsonschema runner this week. Plan:
- Use jsonschema 4.x with Draft-07 semantics and validate with additionalProperties=false.
- Instrument a checklist: parse failures, type mismatches, extra fields, and partial arrays.
- Output a normalized report (CSV row per prompt) with columns: prompt_id, model, pass_bool, error_type, latency_ms, token_count.

I’ll attach a sample run (eval_results.csv) to the Drive once I have the first pass. Also adding a note: for the idempotency test we should surface a deterministic id in the function call so retries don't cause duplicate side-effects.

-Neha

We’ve uploaded a signed DPA and our compliance checklist to the Drive link you shared. If you can confirm the 90-day retention with encryption-at-rest settings before the call that would be ideal.

Looking forward to Thursday 10:00 AM PST.
